gloss: Starting from scratch; building a business without any initial resources.
teaser: Ever wondered how some people build empires from nothing?
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered how some people build empires from nothing? [break 1s] The phrase is: 白手起家, bái shǒu qǐ jiā. [break 0.5s] 白 (bái) - white, pure [break 0.5s] 手 (shǒu) - hand [break 0.5s] 起 (qǐ) - to rise, to start [break 0.5s] 家 (jiā) - home, family, or business [break 1s] So, 白手起家 literally means 'to start a family with bare hands', and figuratively, it means to build something from nothing. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from the idea of someone who lacks any resources or inheritance but still manages to start a business and become successful through hard work and determination. It's often used to highlight the spirit of entrepreneurship and self-reliance in Chinese culture. [break 1.5s] Example one: 他白手起家，建立了自己的公司。 [break 1s] He built his own company from scratch. [break 1s] Example two: 她白手起家，成为了亿万富翁。 [break 1s] She became a billionaire starting from nothing. [break 1s] Example three: 许多人都相信，白手起家是成功的关键。 [break 1s] Many people believe that starting from scratch is the key to success. [break 1s] So, that's 白手起家 — starting from scratch. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
